trajectory_summary: This is a short, mechanical, efficiently-run verify-and-book call with no resistance to overcome. The rep moves through address, homeowner status, roof, utility, credit, and square footage in order and locks a specific appointment day and time. The call is procedurally clean but emotionally thin — no bill was discussed, no interest reason was drawn out, and the customer's unique situation (not yet moved in, paying cash) was acknowledged but never leveraged.

observed_outcome.reasoning: Customer confirmed there is no co-owner ('Just me. Just you.') at 01:41, and a specific day (tomorrow) and time (9AM) were agreed for a phone call, satisfying the booked outcome criteria.

bill_anchor_audit.reasoning: The rep never asks about a bill or usage figure at any point; given the customer hasn't moved into the home yet, there may be no bill history to capture, but the rep also doesn't acknowledge this gap or ask about her current residence's bill for a proxy.

primary_coaching_focus.quote: Is this kind of your first time, looking into solar, or have you looked into it before?
primary_coaching_focus.why: The rep never asks or draws out why this new homeowner wants solar — a one-sentence follow-up here would have given the closer a real motivational anchor instead of a bare fact ('first time in general').

key_moments.quote: Yeah. Looks like we were just giving you a call because we received a request. You're looking at solar for the home. How are you doing today?
key_moments.stewart_read: The rep never states the company's full legitimacy anchor beyond 'Ion' and a vague 'we received a request' — no state framing, no certified-installer language, no reference to the specific form/channel. It works here because the customer is already compliant, but the intro's job of pre-empting 'is this a scam?' is thin.

key_moments.quote: No. That's that makes sense. Yeah. I don't blame you. Is this kind of your first time, looking into solar, or have you looked into it before?
key_moments.stewart_read: This is the closest the rep gets to the required 'what interested you in solar' question, but it's phrased as a yes/no history check rather than an open probe for motivation. The customer answers 'first time... in general' and the rep never follows up on WHY she's interested.

key_moments.quote: Well, you know, you're about to put the aqua plant. So I'm just trying to get prepared before that aqua plant get put up.
key_moments.stewart_read: The customer is a brand-new homeowner about to move in and the rep frames solar planning as getting ahead of the 'aqua plant' (likely a mishearing/transcription of a fence, patio, or similar improvement). This is a timing-alignment enthusiasm signal — a new homeowner planning property changes before moving in is a strong window for solar-inclusive planning.

key_moments.quote: Yes. Because I was still I'm going, doing this cash doing a cash, price deal.
key_moments.stewart_read: The customer raises the credit qualifier only to redirect into a cash-purchase plan — this is a moment where the rep could reinforce that a cash deal is even simpler/faster, tying it forward to the appointment. Instead the rep just acknowledges and moves to square footage.
